title: XR and Digital Experiences for Rehabilitation: Motivation, Engagement, Performance and Experience
summary: Extended Reality (XR), encompassing virtual, augmented, and mixed reality, is increasingly adopted in rehabilitation to enhance treatment effectiveness through immersive, adaptive, and motivating environments. Beyond motor and cognitive outcomes, successful XR-based rehabilitation critically depends on psychological factors such as motivation, engagement, emotional regulation, and perceived experience. At the same time, XR systems enable multimodal data acquisition, including behavioral metrics and neurophysiological signals such as EEG and MRI, offering unprecedented opportunities for objective, continuous, and ecologically valid assessment of psychological, behavioral, and physiological processes. However, the rapid technological development has outpaced the establishment of standardized, quantitative measures capable of capturing both subjective psychological processes and their underlying neural and physiological correlates within rehabilitation contexts.

title: Myotonic Disorders: Myotonic Dystrophies (DM1/DM2) and Non-Dystrophic Myotonias
summary: Myotonic Dystrophies, Non-Dystrophic Myotonias, and related Myotonic Syndromes are complex neuromuscular disorders marked by myotonia, progressive or episodic muscle weakness, and variable multisystem involvement. Beyond skeletal muscle symptoms, affected individuals may experience an important disease burden and reduced quality of life. Myotonic dystrophies (DM1 and DM2), the most prevalent adult-onset muscular dystrophies, are particularly characterized by marked phenotypic variability and multisystem involvement, which complicate early diagnosis, risk stratification, and long-term management. Cardiac, respiratory, endocrine, metabolic, gastrointestinal, ophthalmological, and central nervous system (CNS) manifestations — including cognitive and neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disturbances, fatigue, apathy, hypersomnolence, and anosognosia — profoundly influence morbidity, mortality, functional independence, and quality of life. title: Safe and Trustworthy Reinforcement Learning for Human–Robot Collaboration
summary: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has rapidly emerged as a powerful approach for enabling robots to acquire adaptive, data-driven behaviors in real-world environments. In Human–Robot Interaction (HRI), RL offers a pathway toward robots that can collaborate effectively with people, adapt to user preferences, and operate under changing task and environmental conditions. However, HRI introduces distinct challenges: human behavior is dynamic and diverse, interaction is often partially observable, and many settings are safety-critical and socially constrained. As a result, conventional autonomy pipelines—and RL methods optimized primarily for performance—can struggle to deliver interactions that are safe, predictable, and intuitive, especially under uncertainty and distribution shift.

title: Complex Soccer Motor Skills: Mechanisms, Measurement, and Field Performance
summary: Soccer is one of the world’s most cognitively and motorically demanding team sports, in which match outcomes often depend on a small number of decisive actions. Among these, scoring-related skills are especially important because they emerge under severe temporal pressure, variable environmental constraints, and strong psychological tension. Yet many complex soccer skills, particularly advanced finishing and airborne scoring techniques, remain underexplored scientifically despite their clear practical importance. As a result, coaches often rely on experiential knowledge rather than evidence-based training principles when teaching them. Recent advances in motion capture, wearable sensing, video analytics, and artificial intelligence now offer new opportunities to study these actions in more representative contexts and to generate knowledge that is directly usable in coaching. This Research Topic aims to strengthen the bridge between movement science and real-world soccer practice.

title: Deep learning strategies for multimodal image fusion in neuroimaging
summary: Neuroimaging has become a cornerstone of modern neuroscience, enabling detailed investigation of brain structure, function, and pathology. With advances in imaging modalities such as magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), functional MRI (fMRI), positron emission tomography (PET), and magneto- and electroencephalography (M/EEG), researchers now gather complementary data capturing diverse aspects of brain physiology. However, combining these heterogeneous sources into unified, meaningful representations remains a critical challenge due to differences in spatial resolution, contrast mechanisms, and signal characteristics.

Traditional fault diagnosis methods struggle with high-dimensional, nonlinear data, while data-driven and AI-based approaches offer improved capabilities. Digital twin technology further enhances real-time monitoring and predictive maintenance through virtual–physical synchronization. However, challenges remain in multi-physics modeling, data fusion, model generalization, and ensuring real-time, secure, and scalable deployment in practical environments.

title: Personalised Surgical Care in Neuro-Oncology
summary: The management of brain tumours, particularly diffuse gliomas (WHO grades 2–4), remains one of the most complex challenges in modern neurosurgery. This Research Topic welcomes submissions addressing both adult and paediatric brain tumours, as well as primary and secondary brain tumours, including brain metastases from extracranial solid or haematological malignancies. Their infiltrative growth patterns and frequent proximity to eloquent brain regions often limit the extent of safe resection. While maximal tumour resection, defined radiologically, has consistently been associated with improved outcomes, the benefit of incomplete resection remains uncertain, highlighting the need for careful, individualised surgical decision-making. In many cases, stereotactic biopsy may represent a more appropriate approach when the risks of surgery outweigh potential oncological gains.

title: Complement at the Crossroads: Neuroinflammation vs Neuroprotection in CNS Injury and Disorders
summary: The complement system is a central component of innate immunity and plays a critical role in the central nervous system (CNS), both in normal physiology and across a wide spectrum of neurological conditions. Under homeostatic conditions (notably during brain development), complement contributes to synaptic refinement and clearance of cellular debris. In contrast, chronic or dysregulated complement activation in CNS injury or disease drives neuroinflammation, synapse loss, and neurodegeneration. These effects have been characterized across numerous conditions, including Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI), Spinal Cord Injury (SCI), Alzheimer's Disease (AD), Parkinson's Disease (PD), Stroke, Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), Multiple Sclerosis (MS), and others. Recent advances in understanding complement's dual roles in the CNS have spurred development of targeted therapeutics, several of which are now in clinical trials, though most address rare diseases. title: Towards Trustworthy Visual Foundation Models in the Real World
summary: The recent surge of interest in generative AI has brought unprecedented advances in content generation, reasoning, and multimodal interaction, while also exposing a growing set of concerns that extend well beyond model performance. As generative AI systems are increasingly deployed in real-world scenarios, issues such as fairness, privacy, safety, robustness, transparency, and accountability have become central to their responsible development and use. Although substantial efforts have been made to address these challenges, existing research remains scattered across different communities and often focuses on isolated aspects of the problem. title: Advancing Soft Technology: Innovative Sensing Solutions for Next-Generation Biomedical Applications
summary: Soft and flexible sensors are transforming sensing technologies by addressing the limitations of rigid, traditional systems. Designed to mimic the mechanical properties of biological tissues or adapt to irregular surfaces, these sensors provide enhanced integration and functionality. Built from materials like elastomers, conductive polymers, and hydrogels, they use principles such as resistive, capacitive, optical, and piezoelectric sensing to detect pressure, strain, temperature, and chemical changes. Recent advances include self-healing materials, miniaturized fabrication techniques, wireless electronics, and energy-autonomous systems, enabling durable and multifunctional designs.

Digital Mental Health Interventions in Comorbid Chronic Physical Conditions
summary: Mental health problems are highly prevalent among individuals with chronic physical conditions (e.g., COPD, cardiovascular disease, and diabetes). Individuals with multimorbidity, defined as the co-occurrence of chronic physical conditions and mental health problems, frequently experience elevated psychological distress, including anxiety, depressive symptoms, and emotional strain, alongside the ongoing demands of managing and adapting to long-term illness. These combined challenges can negatively affect coping, daily functioning, and engagement with both psychological and somatic care. At the same time, mental health problems are not always adequately identified or treated, partly due to fragmentation between mental and physical healthcare, resulting in limited integration of psychological support within chronic care pathways.

title: From Digital Well-Being to Online Victimization: New Frontiers in Cyberpsychology
summary: Digital technologies have become deeply embedded in everyday life, shaping the way individuals communicate, form relationships, access information, seek psychological support, and engage with society. Following the COVID-19 pandemic, the use of digital technologies in mental health care, including online counseling and psychotherapy, has increased substantially, highlighting new opportunities for promoting psychological well-being and expanding access to care. At the same time, digital environments expose users to a range of risks, including cyberbullying, cybercrime, online victimization, technology-facilitated violence, and the non-consensual sharing of intimate content. These phenomena have significant implications for mental health, interpersonal relationships, and legal systems. As digital interactions continue to evolve, there is a growing need for interdisciplinary research examining risk and protective factors, prevention strategies, resilience processes, and evidence-based int

title: Multidimensional Evaluation and Multimodal Interventions for Dysphagia, Oral Health, and Nutritional Management in Neurological Diseases - Volume II
summary: Dysphagia constitutes a significant and multifaceted challenge within the realm of neurological disease, frequently emerging alongside oral dysfunction and malnutrition to markedly worsen patient outcomes. This triad not only increases the likelihood of aspiration pneumonia, frailty, and extended hospitalization, but also contributes to increased mortality rates. Growing evidence from recent research underscores the pivotal roles that oral health, oral microbiome dynamics, and nutritional status play in both the onset and progression of dysphagia. While modern clinical practice is rapidly adapting by adopting comprehensive management strategies that encompass the interconnected domains of swallowing, oral care, and diet, important questions remain concerning the optimization and real-world applicability of these interventions.

title: Sensory-motor integration in human movement
summary: For desired and coordinated movements, the central nervous system integrates multiple sensory feedback with motor commands. Optimum integration of multi-sensory signals from visual, vestibular, and somatosensory systems is vital to performing activities of daily life and is commonly compromised due to aging, neuromuscular disorders, and traumatic injuries. Compromised sensor-motor integration can potentially lead to a stability control deficiency, increased risk of falling, tremors, rigidity, and decreased hand dexterity, just to name a few. However, there is a limited understanding of the mechanisms responsible for sensory-motor integration, specifically, how the central nervous system adapts to changes in environmental conditions (e.g., visual input is obstructed), physical and mental health, and cognitive status. A comprehensive study of sensory-motor integration can be beneficial to healthcare professionals, neuroscientists, and human health in general.

title: Cognitive and Mental Health Improvement Under- and Post-COVID-19, volume IV
Competent Emotionality, Creativity and Resilience: New Research Approaches to Address Emotional Distress Through “Caring for Each Other”
summary: Contemporary emotion science is increasingly moving beyond models that frame emotional functioning as an individual skill or stable trait. Competent emotionality offers an alternative perspective, conceptualizing emotional processes as dynamic, relational, and context-dependent capacities. Within this framework, creativity emerges not only as a cognitive ability but as an affective and social process through which individuals make sense of, transform, and respond to their emotional environment. Resilience, in turn, is understood as the distinctive capacity of individuals and communities to absorb adversity and emerge transformed from it. Despite growing evidence on each of these dimensions separately, the affective mechanisms that connect them — and how they jointly shape responses to systemic emotional distress — remain underexplored. This Research Topic addresses this gap by foregrounding the emotional and relational processes through which competent emotionality, creativity, and res

title: Energy, Enzymes, and the Brain: From Cellular Pathways to Therapeutic Pharmacology in Neurological And Neurodegenerative Disorders
summary: Neurodegenerative disorders are pressing global health challenges that stem from progressive neuronal dysfunction and loss. While the central roles of mitochondria in energy production, redox balance, and apoptosis have long been recognized in the context of these conditions, emerging research highlights a fascinating new player: the cytochrome P450 (CYP) superfamily, traditionally studied in hepatic drug metabolism, but now understood as an integral contributor to brain physiology.

Frontiers in Disc-Preserving Minimally Invasive Spine Surgery: Regeneration and Resorption
summary: Herniated disc disease-induced neurological dysfunction has become a significant medical and social issue. Traditional treatment approaches have focused on discectomy and spinal fusion, which inevitably alter the physiological structure and biomechanics of the spine and may lead to adjacent segment degeneration. In the era of precision medicine and minimally invasive surgery, the treatment of herniated discs is shifting toward "structural preservation" and "functional restoration."

title: Motor imagery and action observation for functional recovery and neurorehabilitation
summary: Motor imagery and action observation are movement representation techniques that have received growing attention in neurorehabilitation over recent years. These approaches offer a valuable framework for understanding the neural basis of action representation and motor simulation, while also supporting the development of innovative therapeutic strategies for individuals with neurological disorders and functional limitations. Their increasing relevance in both research and clinical practice reflects a broader interest in the role of simulated and observed action in motor learning, neuroplasticity, and functional recovery.

title: The legacy of Dr. Paul Broca: Expanding views on language processing, Volume II
summary: Neuroscience and linguistics have benefited significantly from the foundational work of Dr. Paul Broca, whose research in the 19th century on the brain’s role in speech production paved the way for a modern understanding of language processing. Broca’s identification of the brain area responsible for coordinated speech movements — a region now termed “Broca’s area” — highlighted the cerebral localization of language function. Despite the advances since Broca’s time, questions linger about the precise mechanisms of speech production and the integration of linguistic processing with neural pathways, suggesting a need for ongoing research.

title: The effects of lithium: from mood stabilization to disease-modifying effects in neurological and psychiatric disorders
summary: Lithium (Li⁺) remains a foundational treatment in psychiatry, particularly for bipolar disorder, manic episodes, and suicide prevention in major depressive disorder and other mood disorders. Although clinically used for decades, its molecular and systems-level mechanisms are not fully resolved. Beyond its psychiatric indications, lithium is increasingly recognized as a regulator of neuronal resilience, with emerging relevance for aging and neurodegenerative disease.

title: New Insight in Criminological and Forensic Neuropsychology
summary: Neuropsychological research has significantly advanced the understanding of cognitive, executive, and affective processes underlying criminal behavior, legal competence, and responsibility. However, the use of neuropsychological evidence in criminological and forensic practice remains fragmented, with limited integration between clinical assessment and judicial decision-making. This Research Topic aims to bring together contributions that advance criminological and forensic neuropsychology from a clearly defined, clinically grounded perspective. The Topic is organized around a forensic neuropsychological through-line, focusing on the assessment and interpretation of cognitive functioning in legally relevant contexts and on translating neuropsychological findings from clinical evaluation to court-related settings.

title: Neuroimaging in stroke
summary: Stroke remains one of the leading causes of death and long-term disability worldwide, posing a substantial burden on healthcare systems and societies. Over the past three decades, neuroimaging has transformed every stage of stroke care, from hyperacute triage and treatment selection to the longitudinal assessment of recovery and secondary prevention. Computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and advanced perfusion and vascular techniques now allow clinicians to visualize the ischemic core, the salvageable penumbra, hemorrhagic transformation, and microstructural tissue injury with unprecedented spatial and temporal resolution. In parallel, the integration of artificial intelligence (AI), and multimodal imaging biomarkers is reshaping how we characterize cerebrovascular pathophysiology, predict clinical outcomes, and personalize therapeutic strategies. title: Alzheimer's disease-associated genes expression: A new direction in the ischemic etiology and therapy of Alzheimer's disease
summary: Increasing evidence supports a link between brain ischemia and the development of Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Experimental and clinical studies have shown that ischemic episodes trigger the overexpression of genes associated with AD pathology, including amyloid precursor protein (APP), β-secretase (BACE1), presenilin 1 and 2, and tau protein. These changes promote beta-amyloid peptide accumulation, neurofibrillary tangle formation, and progressive neurodegeneration in patterns that closely mirror the hallmarks of AD. Despite growing recognition that ischemia-reperfusion injury may represent a critical upstream trigger for AD-type pathology, the molecular cascades linking ischemic gene dysregulation to sustained neurodegeneration remain incompletely understood. This gap limits the development of targeted therapies that could intervene at the vascular and ischemic level to slow or prevent the onset of AD.

title: Imaging Innovations for Enhanced Alzheimer’s Diagnosis
summary: Medical imaging remains an essential field in neurodegenerative disease research, providing critical insights into the structural and functional abnormalities associated with disorders like Alzheimer’s disease. The evolution of imaging technologies has long been central to driving early diagnosis, refining disease classification, and enabling rigorous monitoring of progression or response to therapy. Despite these advances, current imaging techniques often grapple with limitations in sensitivity, contrast, specificity, and the capacity to distinguish Alzheimer’s pathology from other neurodegenerative conditions. There is increasing interest in integrating innovative imaging agents, hybrid modalities, and nanotechnology-based approaches to overcome these challenges. Recent explorations into theranostic agents and multi-functional nanomaterials have set the stage for more precise, non-invasive visualization of disease processes, yet substantial gaps remain regarding optimal materials, de
image_alt: Imaging Innovations for Enhanced Alzheimer’s Diagnosis

title: Microglial Dynamics in Alzheimer's: Genetic Variants and Therapeutic Pathways
summary: Microglia are pivotal players in the neuroinflammatory landscape of Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Accumulating evidence underscores their complex role in modulating amyloid plaque dynamics, neuronal integrity, and synaptic function. Recent genome-wide association and sequencing studies have revealed that the majority of AD risk loci are highly expressed in microglia. Variants in a broad network of microglial genes—including TREM2, ABI3, PLCG2, INPP5D, CD33, SPI1 and the MS4A cluster—can fundamentally alter microglial behavior and reactivity. While activated microglia may drive beneficial amyloid clearance and neuroprotective signaling, they can also contribute to pathological synaptic pruning and chronic neuroinflammation, creating a spectrum of responses that complicates our understanding of their exact role in AD pathogenesis. title: Pyroptosis and Ferroptosis in Non-Neuronal Cells: Triggers and Propagation of Neuroinflammation in Aging
summary: Research in neuroinflammation has increasingly highlighted the role of non-neuronal cells, such as microglia, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, endothelial cells, and infiltrating immune cells, in shaping neural environments during aging and neurodegenerative diseases. Among the diverse mechanisms underlying glial and peripheral immune cell activity, recently characterized forms of regulated cell death, pyroptosis and ferroptosis, have attracted significant attention. Pyroptosis, a pro-inflammatory, gasdermin-mediated process, and ferroptosis, driven by iron-dependent lipid peroxidation, both induce cellular demise accompanied by the release of DAMPs and pro-inflammatory factors. Emerging evidence suggests that these distinct cell death pathways in non-neuronal populations can profoundly influence the initiation and propagation of neuroinflammatory cascades, which in turn impact synaptic function, neuronal survival, and cognitive resilience. AI-Driven Approaches in Mental Health Diagnosis and Treatment
summary: The intersection of informatics and mental health represents a burgeoning field poised to significantly transform the landscape of psychological disorder diagnosis and treatment. Advanced machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) techniques enable researchers to decipher intricate patterns and derive profound insights from vast, complex datasets. Such pioneering approaches promise to enhance the precision of diagnoses, facilitate personalized treatment plans, and markedly improve patient outcomes. This convergence is dismantling traditional barriers between data science, clinical psychology, and neuroscience, fostering the emergence of novel strategies that hold the potential to revolutionize mental health care. Despite these advances, gaps persist in fully integrating these technologies in routine clinical settings, and questions around ethical implications and data privacy demand attention.

title: Addressing the Transposition Challenge in Virtual Reality: Adaptive Scaffolding for Self-Regulation, Cognitive Load, and Emotions in Education
summary: The integration of immersive virtual reality (IVR) in educational contexts marks a substantial shift in learning environments, offering high sensory fidelity and interactive potential. However, as students transition from traditional physical classrooms to virtual settings, they frequently encounter the “Transposition Challenge,” losing access to familiar self-regulatory supports such as notes, clocks, and peer cues. This regulatory void, or “regulatory nakedness,” can elevate extraneous cognitive load and disrupt emotional equilibrium, hindering both engagement and learning outcomes. Recent work—guided by models such as the Cognitive Affective Model of Immersive Learning (CAMIL) and the Cognitive-Affective Theory of Learning with Media for VR (CATLM-VR)—underscores the need for a nuanced understanding of how immersion, embodiment, and interactivity modulate core learning variables including presence, interest, cognitive load, and motivation.

summary: Motivation is widely recognized as a central construct in understanding engagement, persistence, and behavioral change in physical activity and sport contexts. Over several decades, research has generated substantial empirical work examining motivational processes in these settings. At the same time, the broader field of psychological science has increasingly engaged with questions related to research transparency, methodological rigor, and reproducibility. Concerns surrounding incomplete reporting, analytic flexibility, and the limited visibility of research workflows have prompted renewed attention to how studies are designed, conducted, and communicated. Within motivational research on physical activity, these developments highlight the importance of strengthening methodological practices that support transparent research design, robust validation of methods, and reproducible findings. title: Artificial Intelligence for Medical Robotics: From Design Acceleration to Intelligent Perception and Control
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming the field of medical robotics, extending its impact beyond traditional perception and control to earlier stages such as system design and modeling. Emerging approaches leverage machine learning to accelerate computationally intensive processes, including finite element analysis (FEA) for soft and continuum surgical robots and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for medical devices such as blood pumps. In parallel, data-driven methods provide effective alternatives to analytical modeling for complex robotic systems with challenging kinematic and dynamic structures. These advances complement ongoing developments in AI-enabled perception, planning, and intraoperative decision-making. Together, they create new opportunities for improving the efficiency, intelligence, and clinical applicability of medical robotic systems, while also introducing challenges in reliability, interpretability, and integration.

title: Computational modelling and AI for brain and behaviour: integrating prediction with inference
summary: Computational modelling, machine learning, and broader artificial (AI) intelligence approaches are now key approaches used to understanding and predicting cognitive function and behaviour. Although these approaches are closely related, they make distinct contributions. Computational modelling models provide theory driven accounts of cognitive and neural mechanisms. They do that by formalising hypotheses and testing them through algorithms development based on the findings and simulations. In contrast, machine learning and AI methods are successful in discovering structure in complicated and high dimensional data, enabling robust prediction, and supporting analysis across modalities. Together these tools can connect levels of explanation, strengthen inference, and improve reproducibility. Historically computational modelling has been used in computational neuroscience to explain brain processes and behaviour, including neural network and biologically inspired models. Despite these advances, a comprehensive understanding of the complex neural mechanisms underlying these disorders and their clinical progression remains elusive. Recent research highlights the value of AI approaches, including machine learning, deep learning, and generative models, in extracting meaningful patterns from multimodal neuroimaging and genomic data. title: Epidemiology of Multiple sclerosis and related disorders
summary: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a leading cause of non-traumatic neurologic disability in young adults worldwide. Marked variation in incidence and prevalence across geographic regions, ancestry groups, and sexes supports a multifactorial etiology in which genetic susceptibility interacts with environmental exposures. Recent syntheses suggest MS incidence and prevalence have increased over time, often driven by higher rates among women, yet these trends are not uniformly observed and are incompletely characterized in several regions, including the Middle East and North Africa (MENA), where newer data suggest a rapidly rising burden.

title: Future of Theoretical and Philosophical Psychology
summary: Psychological science is at a crossroads. The last two decades has brought a range of fundamental issues into focus, including the replication crisis highlighted by large-scale community efforts such as the Open Science Collaboration, problems with representativeness and diversity emphasized by researchers such as Apicella, Norenzayan, and Henrich, and concerns regarding the very nature of the construction of theories raised by Oberauer and Lewandowsky; and van Rooij and Baggio, and more recent contributions by van Dongen and colleagues. At the same time, long-standing questions about explanation, evidence, and mind-world relations are now intersecting with rapid developments in cognitive science, neuroscience, and artificial intelligence. These converging trends highlight both the urgency and the opportunity for rigorous theoretical and philosophical work that can clarify, critique, and guide the future of psychology.

title: How Does the Environment Modulate Feeding and Metabolism in Fish? Special Emphasis on the Impacts of Climate Change
summary: Feeding and metabolism in fish are vital physiological processes regulated by interactions between internal endocrine signals and external environmental cues. Fish are highly sensitive to environmental parameters such as temperature, oxygen availability, salinity, photoperiod, pollution, and food quality. These variables influence feeding behavior, nutrient assimilation, and energy allocation. The regulation of these functions involves an endocrine network that integrates signals from the brain, gut, liver, and adipose tissue. Hormones such as neuropeptide Y (NPY), agouti-related peptide (AgRP), CART, orexin, leptin, ghrelin, insulin, thyroid hormones, melanocortins, and insulin-like growth factors (IGFs) play central roles in modulating appetite and metabolism.

summary: Literacy acquisition and related disorders stand at the intersection of neuroscience, psychology, and education, forming a convergent field that investigates how brain systems support the development of literacy skills. Recent research has greatly advanced our understanding of the neural and cognitive substrates underlying reading, highlighting the complex interplay between speech perception, phonological processing, orthographic knowledge, and language comprehension. Yet, significant questions remain regarding how these processes coalesce to foster successful reading development and precisely how disruptions in these systems lead to disorders such as dyslexia. Notably, gaps persist in mapping the developmental trajectories of brain networks for reading, elucidating cross-linguistic differences, and translating mechanistic insights into practical frameworks for intervention and education.

title: Music and the Brain: From Neural Mechanisms to Clinical Applications
summary: The field of music neuroscience explores how music engages complex brain networks, making it a uniquely powerful tool for investigating neural processes that underpin perception, action, emotion, prediction, and reward. Recent advances in neuroscience demonstrate that music activates widespread brain systems, from the auditory cortex to motor and reward networks, enabling the study of core principles such as neural entrainment, oscillatory timing, and predictive processing. Large-scale, multimodal studies have begun to illuminate how music can serve as both a model for basic brain function and as a pathway for understanding neurological and psychiatric disorders. Yet, critical gaps persist in linking circuit-level findings to clinically meaningful outcomes, elucidating moderators across development, and leveraging music as a precision tool for diagnosis and intervention.

Transforming Genitourinary Surgery Through Advanced Robotic Systems
summary: The field of genitourinary (GU) surgery has undergone a transformative shift with the integration of robotic technology, which now serves as a cornerstone for minimally invasive procedures. Robotic approaches have been lauded for improved dexterity, enhanced visualization, and better ergonomics for surgeons, leading to increasing adoption. Despite their technical promise, clinical debates remain around appropriate patient selection, comparative benefits over other minimally invasive modalities, and the economic implications of broader deployment. title: Understanding aging and neurodevelopmental change in autistic adults: Language and cognition at the crossroads
summary: The study of aging in adults with autism, particularly in relation to language and cognitive challenges, represents a rapidly evolving field within neurodevelopmental and gerontological research. While much effort has been devoted to understanding autism spectrum disorder (ASD) in childhood, there is a notable lack of comprehensive research that tracks the experiences of autistic individuals as they age. Key questions remain about how typical aging processes interact with lifelong neurodevelopmental conditions, including issues such as the trajectory of language skills, changes in cognitive abilities, and the impact of co-occurring medical conditions. Recent studies suggest that autistic adults might experience aging differently than neurotypical peers, with possible variations in cognitive decline, language processing, and social communication. However, much of the existing work is cross-sectional and lacks longitudinal depth, making it challenging to fully capture the nuanced interpl
image_alt: Understanding aging and neurodevelopmental change in autistic adults: Language and cognition at the crossroads

title: Microbiome and Neuropsychiatric Health: Precision and Predictive Translational Strategies in the Gut-Brain Axis
summary: Over the past decade, the gut microbiome has emerged as a key modulator of brain function, shaping emotion regulation, cognition, stress physiology, and neuroinflammatory pathways. Altered microbiome-host interactions are linked to psychiatric and neurological conditions including depression, anxiety disorders, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, neurodevelopmental conditions, and stress-related syndromes. Despite rapid scientific progress, major challenges remain in clarifying causal mechanisms and successfully translating these discoveries into clinically actionable diagnostics, biomarkers, and therapeutic strategies.

title: Automated and AI-driven analysis techniques in PET brain imaging
summary: Positron emission tomography (PET) brain imaging is a pivotal tool in neuroscience, enabling precise visualization and quantification of physiological processes in the human brain. However, traditional analysis of PET brain images relies heavily on manual workflows and expert interpretation, which can be both time-consuming and susceptible to inter- and intra-observer variability. The need for more robust, reproducible, and efficient analysis techniques has prompted considerable interest in automation and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven approaches. Recent advancements in machine learning, particularly deep learning, have demonstrated the potential to automate complex image processing tasks, improve diagnostic accuracy, and extract clinically relevant biomarkers from PET data. Despite these breakthroughs, integrating AI into clinical practice faces considerable hurdles, including the need for large annotated datasets, generalizability across diverse populations, and transparency in
image_alt: Automated and AI-driven analysis techniques in PET brain imaging

title: Bioactive phytochemicals with neuroimmunopharmacological properties
summary: Plants constitute a vast and still incompletely characterized reservoir of biologically active compounds. Among them are highly potent therapeutic agents such as paclitaxel, employed in oncology, and morphine, a cornerstone of severe pain management. Moreover, numerous plant-derived products contain complex phytochemical compositions that contribute to the maintenance of physiological homeostasis and may play a preventive role in the early stages of disease development. Accordingly, plant-derived substances – including crude extracts, enriched fractions, or isolated compounds – may be considered as valuable candidates for the development of therapeutics, dietary supplements, or functional food components. In any case, these substances exert measurable biological effects by modulating physiological functioning and molecular pathways.

title: Upper-Limb Sensorimotor Function as a Marker of Cognitive Aging
summary: The field of aging neuroscience has increasingly recognized the complex interplay between motor function, tactile sensory function, and cognitive processes across the human lifespan. With global populations aging rapidly, there is heightened interest in finding sensitive and accessible markers that can indicate early cognitive decline or differentiate typical versus pathological aging. Recent studies have revealed that upper-limb sensorimotor abilities—such as hand dexterity, fine motor control, tactile sensation/perception, and coordination—show strong associations with executive functions, memory, as well as global cognitive health in older adults. Longitudinal and intervention research suggests that changes in upper-limb sensorimotor performance may precede, predict, or co-occur with declines in cognitive domains, making these functions a promising, underutilized window into neurocognitive aging. However, the precise mechanisms linking sensorimotor deficits and cognitive changes, th

Beyond Traditional Risk Factors: Unraveling Residual Vascular Risk After TIA and Minor Stroke
summary: Transient ischemic attack (TIA) and minor ischemic stroke are critical warning events that precede disabling strokes and major cardiovascular complications. While traditional risk factors (TRFs) — hypertension, diabetes, hypercholesterolemia, smoking, and atrial fibrillation — are well-established drivers of cerebrovascular disease, a growing body of evidence indicates that a substantial proportion of patients presenting with TIA or minor stroke carry none of these conventional risks. Strikingly, recent data from large international cohorts such as TIAregistry.org demonstrate that recurrent stroke rates in this population are comparable to those seen in patients with TRFs, particularly within the first year after the index event. This observation points to the existence of poorly understood, non-traditional mechanisms that contribute to residual vascular risk and recurrent cerebrovascular events.

title: Brain-inspired learning and adaptation in large models
summary: Recent advances in large-scale AI models, including large language and vision-language-action models, have significantly expanded the capabilities of artificial systems in perception, reasoning, and decision-making. However, these models remain limited in their ability adapt continuously, learn from limited data, and operate reliably in dynamic, real-world environments. In contrast, biological systems exhibit remarkable adaptability through mechanisms such as neural plasticity, efficient coding, and modular organization. This Research Topic focuses on the intersection of neuroscience principles and large-scale AI, exploring how brain-inspired mechanisms can address these limitations and support the development of more flexible and resilient intelligent systems.

title: AI in Human Neuroscience, Ethically Done: Neuroethical Risks, Safeguards, and Governance
summary: Artificial intelligence is revolutionizing human neuroscience, enabling unprecedented advances in brain imaging analysis, neural decoding, predictive modeling, and personalized neurological interventions. However, the rapid integration of AI into neuroscience research and clinical applications raises critical ethical concerns that remain inadequately addressed. These include privacy vulnerabilities with neural data, algorithmic bias in brain-based diagnostic tools, issues of informed consent in AI-driven neuroscience studies, and the potential misuse of neural information for non-medical purposes. As AI systems become increasingly sophisticated and widely deployed, there is an urgent need for comprehensive frameworks that balance scientific innovation with robust ethical safeguards. This Research Topic brings together neuroscientists, ethicists, technologists, and policymakers to advance the responsible integration of AI in human neuroscience.

title: Advancing Critical Military Suicide Studies: Challenging Assumptions and Innovating Prevention
summary: Suicide among military servicemembers and veterans is a profound and persistent public health challenge, manifesting across national and cultural contexts. Despite systematic surveillance, targeted research, and significant resource allocation over the past two decades, suicide rates within military and veteran populations have increased or remained elevated in many Western countries. Historically, efforts have concentrated on the identification of risk and protective factors, the development of clinical interventions, and the implementation of broad institutional prevention strategies. While substantial advancements have been made in clinical, policy, and programmatic domains, a deep-seated paradox persists: investments in conventional prevention strategies have not consistently produced meaningful reductions in suicide deaths or been sufficiently responsive to the unique needs of the military and veteran community, highlighting gaps in our theoretical and practical approaches.

title: Growing Up Online: Social media, smartphones, and the adolescent brain, body, behavior loop
summary: Adolescence is a critical developmental period marked by profound changes in brain architecture, social cognition, and identity formation. Simultaneously, today's adolescents are the first generation to grow up immersed in social media and smartphone technology from early childhood. While digital platforms offer unprecedented opportunities for connection, learning, and self-expression, their rapid integration into adolescent life has raised significant concerns about potential neurobehavioral consequences. Emerging evidence suggests that social media use may impact dopaminergic reward pathways, sleep-wake cycles, attention regulation, and social-emotional development. Additionally, smartphones and digital content influence physical activity, body image, peer relationships, and mental health outcomes. Understanding the complex, bidirectional relationships between digital technology use and adolescent neurodevelopment is essential for identifying risks, promoting resilience, and supporti

title: Neuroscience of learning: How the brain adapts and changes, Volume II
summary: The human brain is remarkably dynamic, constantly adapting to new experiences and environmental changes. This plasticity underlies our capacity to learn throughout the lifespan, shaping how we acquire knowledge and develop new skills. Recent advances in neuroscience have illuminated the cellular, molecular, and network-level changes that support learning, revealing a complex interplay between genetic, neurochemical, and experiential factors. Understanding these mechanisms provides crucial insights into cognitive development, educational strategies, and interventions for learning disorders, making the neuroscience of learning a vibrant and relevant field of research.

title: The Future of Brain Imaging: Techniques and Applications
summary: Brain imaging technologies have been instrumental in advancing our understanding of neural structure, function, and connectivity. Established techniques such as MRI, fMRI, PET, and EEG have provided invaluable insights into brain organization and dynamics in both health and disease. However, the field is rapidly evolving with the emergence of innovative imaging modalities and methodological refinements. Next-generation approaches—including ultra-high field imaging, multimodal integration, real-time imaging, functional ultrasound, and AI-enhanced analysis pipelines—promise unprecedented spatial and temporal resolution. These advances are expanding the frontiers of what we can measure and understand about the human brain, while simultaneously presenting new challenges in data interpretation, standardization, and clinical translation. This Research Topic explores the current state and future trajectory of brain imaging science.

title: The interplay between economic and biopsychosocial factors in brain health
summary: Financial well-being is a strong determinant of human. Individuals from lower socioeconomic backgrounds encounter a disproportionate amount of chronic stress, limited access to resources, and reduced opportunities for cognitive stimulation, all of which can profoundly influence brain development and functioning across the lifespan. At the same time, biological factors (e.g., genetic and biomarker-based risk factors), cognitive function and numerical abilities, and mental health variables like depression and anxiety, can influence an individual's ability to acquire and manage financial resources. There is likely a reciprocal relationship between financial well-being and the brain. Despite growing interest in this field, the bidirectional mechanisms linking economic factors to brain functioning, and health remain poorly understood.

title: Translational research of occupational therapy and psychiatric rehabilitation, Volume IV
summary: The field of occupational therapy (OT) has long recognized the importance of addressing mental health issues to improve overall well-being and functionality in individuals. Despite significant advancements, there remains a critical gap between basic scientific discoveries and their practical application in clinical settings. This gap underscores the need for translational research in the mental health domain of occupational therapy. Translational research serves as a bridge, facilitating the transfer of knowledge from fundamental research into real-world therapeutic interventions that can be effectively utilized by practitioners and benefit patients.

title: Updates on the Management of Glioblastoma Volume II
summary: Glioblastoma (GBM) remains the most common malignant primary brain tumor in adults and is associated with profound neurologic morbidity and a poor overall prognosis despite multimodal therapy. While maximal safe resection followed by radiotherapy and temozolomide remains the cornerstone of care, GBM’s intratumoral heterogeneity, adaptive resistance mechanisms, and the complex, dynamic tumor microenvironment continue to limit durable responses and complicate translation of promising preclinical findings into clinical benefit.
image_alt: Updates on the Management of Glioblastoma Volume II

title: Beyond the Average Brain: Person-Specific Mechanisms and Within-Person Prediction
summary: Traditional neuroscience research has relied on group-level analyses, identifying average patterns across populations. However, substantial heterogeneity exists in brain structure, function, connectivity, and neurobiology across individuals. This variability is not merely noise but reflects meaningful differences in genetics, development, experience, and biology that shape cognition and behavior. Person-specific (idiographic) approaches and within-person prediction models recognize that individuals follow unique neural trajectories and respond differently to interventions. Recent advances in computational modeling, machine learning, intensive longitudinal designs, and single-subject neuroimaging enable detailed characterization of individual brain patterns and their behavioral correlates. Precision neuroscience—tailored to the individual—promises more accurate prediction, more effective interventions, and deeper mechanistic understanding of brain-behavior relationships.

title: Developmental Signaling Pathways at the Intersection of Brain Aging and Neuro-Oncology: Biomarkers, Microenvironment, and Translational Implications
summary: Developmental signaling pathways, including Wnt, Notch, Hedgehog, PI3K/AKT/mTOR, TGF-β, and MAPK, serve as master regulators of neural specification, synaptic plasticity, and tissue homeostasis throughout life. Increasing evidence identifies these conserved molecular networks as a unifying biological framework linking neurodevelopment, brain aging, neurodegeneration, and neuro-oncology. Notably, many of the same signaling pathways that are hyperactivated in brain tumors to promote proliferation, invasion, and therapy resistance become dysregulated in Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s, and Huntington’s diseases, often leading to opposing cellular outcomes: sustained growth and survival in cancer versus dysfunction, senescence, and cell death in neurodegeneration. image_alt: Developmental Signaling Pathways at the Intersection of Brain Aging and Neuro-Oncology: Biomarkers, Microenvironment, and Translational Implications

title: Multisensory Integration in Aging: Implications for Cognitive, Motor, and Brain Health
summary: Multisensory integration (MSI) plays a critical role in perception, action, cognition, and emotion across the adult lifespan. While age-related changes in unisensory processing have been comprehensively documented, accumulating evidence suggests that changes in multisensory processing are not simply secondary consequences of sensory decline. We propose a special collection that aims to bring together diverse experimental, neuroimaging, and interventional approaches aimed at examining how MSI changes with aging, how such changes are related to cognitive and affective vulnerability, and how compensatory mechanisms may support functional performance in older adults.
image_alt: Multisensory Integration in Aging: Implications for Cognitive, Motor, and Brain Health

title: Neural control of locomotion in daily life: Gait variability, stability, and adaptability
summary: Locomotion is one of the most fundamental relevant motor behaviours in humans. Walking in daily life is rarely the steady, cyclical activity often examined in laboratory settings; rather, it requires continuous adjustments to varying terrains, environmental demands, cognitive loads, and concurrent tasks. The neural control of locomotion therefore involves a distributed network spanning spinal central pattern generators, brainstem locomotor regions, the cerebellum, the basal ganglia, and cortical areas, all of which interact dynamically with sensory feedback to produce gait patterns that are simultaneously stable, variable, and adaptable. Gait variability reflects the inherent fluctuations of step-to-step parameters, stability refers to the capacity to resist or recover from perturbations, and adaptability denotes the ability to flexibly modify gait in response to changing internal and external conditions. image_alt: Neural control of locomotion in daily life: Gait variability, stability, and adaptability

title: Neuroactive microbial metabolites and human brain function: mechanisms, biomarkers, and clinical implications
summary: In the rapidly evolving field of neurogastroenterology, mounting evidence highlights the profound influence of neuroactive microbial metabolites on human brain function. The gut-brain axis has become a focal point for understanding how metabolites produced by gut microbiota, reshaped by factors such as diet, medications, and stress, interact with the central nervous system. Recent studies have delineated pathways by which short-chain fatty acids, tryptophan metabolites, bile acids, and other molecules alter blood–brain barrier integrity, microglial activation, neurotransmitter systems, and neural connectivity. Despite promising insights, critical questions remain regarding the reproducibility of findings, individual susceptibility, and translation to clinical practice. There remains a significant gap in mapping specific metabolite signatures to neuropsychiatric phenotypes, as well as understanding how genetic and environmental factors modulate these effects.

title: Brain Iron in Neuropsychiatric Disorders
summary: Iron plays an essential role in neurodevelopment and the physiological functions of the brain by acting as a cofactor for enzymes involved in myelinogenesis, neurotransmitter synthesis, cellular respiration, and antioxidant defense. Iron deficiency hinders neurodevelopment, leading to cognitive, motor, and social performance deficits. Conversely, iron overload contributes to the formation of reactive oxygen species that induce oxidative stress and neuronal dysfunction. Abnormal iron levels also impact neurotransmitter systems by affecting synthesis and receptor activity. Brain iron imbalance has been reported in several neuropsychiatric disorders, highlighting the fundamental implications of this metal in mental health. However, the specific neurobiological and molecular pathways linking iron to neuropsychiatric disorders are only beginning to be elucidated. Understanding these mechanisms can have major clinical implications for the treatment of neuropsychiatric disorders and the manag
image_alt: Brain Iron in Neuropsychiatric Disorders

title: The Endocannabinoid System as an Adaptive Hub: Beyond Canonical Cannabinoids in Neuropharmacology
summary: The endocannabinoid system (ECS) is increasingly recognized not merely as a receptor–ligand signaling pathway, but as a dynamic integrative network that coordinates neural, immune, and metabolic responses to environmental challenges. In the central nervous system, the ECS plays a crucial role in adaptive processes related to stress resilience, neuroinflammation, immune competence, and synaptic plasticity. While early pharmacological strategies predominantly focused on direct agonism or antagonism of cannabinoid receptors, clinical translation has been hindered by safety concerns, limited specificity, and context-independent modulation. Emerging evidence now suggests that functionally tuning the ECS, rather than globally activating or blocking it, may represent a more effective and physiologically aligned therapeutic approach.

title: Towards Autonomous and Trustworthy Robotic Systems: Intelligent Control, Motion Planning, and Embodied Decision-Making
summary: Intelligent control and planning constitute the decision-making core of modern robotic systems, enabling autonomous operation, adaptive behaviors, and optimized task execution in complex, dynamic environments. As robotics advances toward higher levels of autonomy, the synergy between perception, decision-making, and motion generation has become increasingly vital. In this context, sophisticated control and planning algorithms not only enhance operational efficiency but also empower robots to safely interact and adapt within unpredictable real-world scenarios.

Although considerable advances have been made in acute care and neurorehabilitation, these disturbances remain among the most disabling and challenging consequences of ABI.

title: Long-Term Outcomes of Critically Ill Patients with Acute Brain Injury
summary: Neurocritical care has evolved into a discipline with clear benefits, with organised services linked to lower mortality and better functional outcomes. Yet, many survivors of acute brain injury (ABI) admitted to intensive care units continue to experience significant physical, cognitive, and emotional impairments long after discharge. Despite advances in acute management, long-term recovery trajectories remain poorly characterised, often measured by crude or inconsistent metrics that overlook patients’ quality of life and day-to-day functioning. Current evidence highlights a pressing need for better tools, standardised follow-up, and more nuanced understanding of how these patients recover over time and across different healthcare contexts.

title: Natural Products for Alzheimer's Disease, Depression, and Related Disorders: From Discovery to Mechanisms
summary: The incidence and mortality rates of neurological diseases are increasing annually, with a trend toward affecting younger populations, severely impacting patients' quality of life and exacerbating the societal healthcare burden. These diseases encompass neurodegenerative disorders such as Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease, as well as various other types including depression and dementia due to cerebrovascular disease. Their pathogenesis is complex, involving neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, apoptosis, endoplasmic reticulum stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, deficiency in brain-derived neurotrophic factor, and reduced cholinergic activity. Natural products, as the oldest source of medicines, continue to provide crucial support for new drug development due to their rich chemical and functional diversity. Multiple modern pharmacological studies have shown that natural product active molecules such as flavonoids and organic acids have good therapeutic effects on neurological

title: Safety Critical Intelligent Control of Systems with Uncertain Dynamical Models
summary: Intelligent control has become a cornerstone of modern robotics and autonomous systems, where agents must operate safely and reliably despite uncertainty in their dynamics, environments, and sensing. From autonomous vehicles and aerial drones to robotic manipulators and assistive medical devices, the integration of adaptive, learning-based, and data-driven controllers has expanded the capabilities of these systems to function in highly dynamic contexts. However, achieving formal safety and stability guarantees within such frameworks remains a crucial and unsolved challenge. Uncertainties due to unmodeled dynamics, sensor noise, or real-time learning processes can threaten mission-critical reliability—especially when systems must make autonomous decisions without human oversight.

title: Multisensory Learning: XR, AI, and Cognitive Performance
summary: Extended reality (XR), including augmented reality (AR), mixed reality (MR), and virtual reality (VR), is moving learning research beyond screen-based presentation toward situated environments in which learners see, hear, smell, touch, move, collaborate, and receive adaptive feedback. These environments create new opportunities to examine learning as a multisensory, embodied, and socially mediated process across formal and informal contexts. At the same time, artificial intelligence and multimodal learning analytics are making it possible to model interaction traces that were previously difficult to interpret, including gaze, gesture, speech, motion, physiological signals, and haptic or olfactory engagement. However, much XR learning research still treats immersion as a broad intervention rather than examining how specific sensory cues and interaction patterns shape cognition, affect, attention, memory, spatial reasoning, motivation, and performance. A more precise psychological accoun
image_alt: Multisensory Learning: XR, AI, and Cognitive Performance

title: Decoding Gene–Environment Interaction in Psychiatric Disorders: From Cross-Disorder Genetic Architecture to Precision Psychiatry
summary: Psychiatric disorders are highly heritable yet profoundly shaped by environmental exposures, with increasing evidence suggesting that shared genetic architectures underlie multiple diagnostic categories. Large-scale genome-wide association studies (GWAS), biobank resources, and advances in statistical genetics have revealed extensive pleiotropy and genetic correlations across disorders such as schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, major depressive disorder, substance use disorders, and suicidality. Meanwhile, environmental risk factors—including early-life adversity, substance exposure, stress, and social determinants—modulate genetic susceptibility through complex gene–environment (G×E) interactions. Recent developments in multi-ancestry genomics, polygenic risk modeling, multi-omics integration, and longitudinal cohort designs now provide unprecedented opportunities to dissect how genetic liability and environmental contexts jointly shape psychiatric phenotypes, disease trajectories, and

title: Multisensory interactions in speech and language: from theory to application
summary: Speech and language perception are inherently multisensory processes. The integration of auditory, visual, and somatosensory signals plays a fundamental role in how humans process and produce language across the lifespan. From the classic McGurk effect to the role of gesture in communication, converging evidence highlights that the brain does not process speech in isolation — rather, it continuously combines input across modalities to build robust and flexible linguistic representations. Despite significant advances in cognitive neuroscience, psycholinguistics, and computational modelling, key questions remain regarding the neural mechanisms underlying multisensory speech integration, how these processes break down in clinical populations, and how they can be harnessed in real-world applications.

In addition, neuropsychiatric manifestations such as apathy, depression, sleep disturbances, and reduced cognitive flexibility frequently emerge during aging and may precede or accompany neurodegenerative disorders.

title: Working memory mechanisms in speech and language acquisition and processing
summary: Working memory plays a central role in the cognitive and neural systems that support speech and language acquisition. It sustains transient representations of sounds, words, and syntactic structures, allowing learners to form stable linguistic knowledge while supporting the online processing of linguistic information during comprehension and production. Current neuroscience findings reveal that working memory is not a unitary construct but involves a dynamic interaction of the fronto-parietal control network, dorsal and ventral language streams, hippocampus, and cerebellum. Techniques such as high-resolution fMRI, MEG, intracranial recordings, and naturalistic neuroimaging have delineated how these distributed regions synchronize during word learning and sentence processing. Digital Mental Health for People with Chronic Conditions: experiences, impact and interventions
summary: About 60% of people live with a chronic illness, such as eczema, epilepsy or a cleft lip. This ranges from 25% in children to 96% in people aged 75 and older. A chronic illness is defined as a condition that lasts longer than three months, recurs more than three times a year and/or is related to long-term use of medication, treatment or help (van Hal et al., 2019). According to the WHO, chronic conditions are conditions that require ongoing management over a period of years or decades. Living with a chronic illness often involves facing recurrent or long-term physical health issues, frequent medical treatment, and ongoing medication use. These experiences, alongside social and psychological stressors, contribute to an elevated risk of mental health difficulties, including depression, anxiety, and body image concerns.

title: Human-AI Symbiosis in the Workplace: Cognitive, Affective, and Relational Dynamics of Intelligent Collaboration
summary: While artificial intelligence is reshaping the workplace at an unprecedented pace, the psychological experience of working alongside AI remains poorly understood. AI now serves as a decision-support tool, collaborator, communication partner, and algorithmic management system across a wide range of organizational contexts. Existing studies have paid considerable attention to AI adoption, productivity improvement, and ethical risks, but less attention has been paid to the psychological dynamics through which employees experience, interpret, and adapt to intelligent collaboration in their everyday work. Human-AI collaboration is not merely a technological arrangement; it also involves cognitive sensemaking, emotional responses, trust calibration, autonomy negotiation, identity reconstruction, and relational adjustments within teams and organizations. Understanding these processes helps explain under what conditions AI can enhance human capabilities, and under what conditions it may genera

title: Large Language Models in Neuroinformatics
summary: Large Language Models (LLMs), such as GPT, LLaMA, Gemini, and other frontier and open-weight transformer-based architectures, are revolutionising how we represent and process information. In neuroscience, the application of LLMs has begun to unlock powerful new capabilities, from decoding brain activity to automating data annotation and enhancing literature-based discovery.

title: Psychological Health and Safety at Work: A Systems-Level Approach to Psychosocial Risk, Organizational Context, and Employee Well-Being
summary: Psychological health and safety (PHS) has emerged as a critical priority in contemporary workplaces, reflecting growing recognition of psychosocial risks such as excessive workload, job insecurity, and poor organizational support. Traditionally, research on employee well-being has focused on individual-level stress and coping; however, there is increasing emphasis on organizational and system-level determinants of mental health at work. Frameworks such as the Job Demands–Resources (JD-R) model and psychosocial safety climate (PSC) highlight how work design, leadership, and human resource practices shape both risk and protective factors. Recent developments, including international standards such as ISO 45003, further underscore the need for integrated approaches to managing psychological health and safety. This Research Topic builds on this shift by examining how organizational systems create, sustain, or mitigate psychosocial risk and influence employee well-being.

title: Resilience and Psychological Recovery in Times of Stress and Uncertainty: Pathways to Mental Health and Human Flourishing
summary: The field of psychological resilience and adaptation has gained increasing relevance in recent years as individuals and societies face persistent stressors ranging from global crises to personal hardships. Research has illuminated the complex interplay between biological, psychological, and social processes that underpin human responses to adversity. Despite an expanding body of evidence, questions remain about how people rebuild wellbeing after disruption, the mechanisms that sustain recovery, and the factors that distinguish mere survival from genuine flourishing. Emerging studies challenge traditional deficit-oriented frameworks and instead highlight dynamic models of growth, flexibility, and meaning-making. Yet, gaps persist in understanding how contextual, cultural, and temporal factors influence the trajectories of psychological recovery and personal development.

title: Sleep as a Regulator of Stress and Emotion: Neurobiological Mechanisms of a Bidirectional Relationship
summary: Sleep and the brain’s capacity to process stress and regulate emotion are deeply intertwined. Psychosocial and physiological stressors disrupt sleep architecture, while disrupted sleep in turn impairs emotional regulation, threat appraisal, and stress coping. Although this bidirectional relationship is well-documented behaviourally and clinically, the underlying neurobiological mechanisms - spanning molecular, cellular, and circuit-level processes - remain incompletely understood.

title: Tetracyclines and their Non-Antibiotic Derivatives: Therapeutic Potential in Neurodegeneration and Neuronal Dysfunction
summary: Neurodegenerative disorders arise from interconnected pathological cascades involving neuroinflammation, protein misfolding, and progressive neuronal dysfunction. These processes, often exacerbated by aging, lead to irreversible declines in neural plasticity and resilience. In recent years, tetracyclines and their non-antibiotic derivatives have emerged as pharmacologically versatile molecules with strong potential for neuroprotection. Beyond their classical antibacterial effects, these compounds mitigate glial activation, suppress pro-inflammatory cytokine production, inhibit ferroptosis, and prevent protein aggregation, thereby targeting critical mechanisms underlying neurodegenerative progression. Despite these promising findings, it remains unclear how their molecular profiles interact with age-related changes in neuroimmune regulation, proteostasis, and metabolic homeostasis. title: The Role of the Cerebellum in Neurocognitive Disorders
summary: The cerebellum, historically linked only to motor control, is now recognized as a vital hub for executive function, emotion, and social cognition. Through dense, reciprocal loops, the cerebellum connects with prefrontal, temporal, and parietal areas to modulate thinking and attention. Disruptions in these networks contribute to several neurocognitive disorders. These include Alzheimer’s disease, frontotemporal dementia, vascular dementia, and mixed cognitive decline. Yet, we still do not fully understand structural, functional, and metabolic changes in specific cerebellar subregions. We also need to map how these changes manifest in patients. Advanced imaging tools like positron emission tomography (PET), multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and quantitative radiomics can map these alterations in vivo. They connect subtle cerebellar pathology with network dysconnectivity and cognitive decline. Studying these links helps us find early disease markers. It also helps us under

title: Artificial Intelligence and Assistive Robotics: Socio-Psychological and Educational Implications
summary: In recent years, AI and robotic systems have begun to transition from controlled laboratory settings into everyday contexts such as education, healthcare and assistive care. These technologies show potential for enabling adaptive learning, personalized support and social interaction, reshaping how individuals engage with digital systems. Socially Assistive Robots (SARs), in particular, have been explored in therapeutic and educational settings, suggesting positive effects on engagement, communication and socio-emotional development, especially among vulnerable populations such as children with autism. While there is a growing body of work in this direction, the practical deployment of SARs and AI in real-world settings remains limited and has not reached widespread adoption.

title: Innovative applications of fNIRS in brain and behavioral studies
summary: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) offers a unique combination of temporal resolution, ecological validity, and practical flexibility that complements and, in many contexts, surpasses the constraints of traditional neuroimaging approaches. fNIRS enables continuous, non-invasive monitoring of cortical hemodynamics with minimal susceptibility to motion artifacts — a critical advantage when studying populations and behaviors that are incompatible with conventional laboratory settings.

title: Selfhood and Consciousness: Bodily, Narrative, and Minimal Dimensions of the Conscious Self
Targeting Neuroinflammation: Mechanisms, Pathways and Therapeutic Opportunities
summary: Neuroinflammation is a critical pathological process at the intersection of immunology and neuroscience. It is now established as a key driver in the onset and progression of a wide range of central nervous system (CNS) disorders, including Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s disease, multiple sclerosis, traumatic brain injury, and depression. The complex interplay between activated glial cells, inflammatory signaling, and neuronal function presents both a significant challenge and a compelling opportunity for therapeutic intervention. Despite significant advances in understanding these mechanisms, effective pharmacological treatments targeting neuroinflammation remain scarce outside of broad immunosuppressive approaches.

title: Critical perspectives on gendered mental health issues/women’s mental health
summary: Objectives: • To publish examples of excellent interdisciplinary work on women’s mental health • To encourage conceptual frameworks for approaching women’s mental health as an interdisciplinary and intersectional problem • To contribute to new ways of tackling the gendered mental illness gap as a longstanding and life long health problem • To highlight reproductive transitional periods that are unique to women, including the perinatal period and perimenopause, as important contexts for interdisciplinary mental health research

title: From 5G to Satellite: AI Approaches for Energy-Efficient, High-Performance Network Infrastructures
summary: The exponential growth in data traffic, driven by 5G/6G rollout, cloud computing, real-time applications, and massive IoT deployment, places increasing strain on high-speed network infrastructures. Conventional, rule-based network management cannot adapt quickly enough to dynamic traffic patterns, resulting in inefficient energy use and degraded performance. Artificial intelligence, including deep reinforcement learning, federated learning, graph neural networks, and large language models, offers a path toward networks that self-optimize, predict demand, and conserve energy without sacrificing throughput or latency.
image_alt: From 5G to Satellite: AI Approaches for Energy-Efficient, High-Performance Network Infrastructures

title: Robotics at a Crossroads: AI-Based vs Classical Methods in Control, HRI, and Autonomy
summary: The field of robotics is undergoing a profound transformation driven by rapid advances in artificial intelligence, particularly large language models and vision-language models. These AI-based approaches are increasingly being integrated into robotic systems for control, decision-making, perception, and human-robot interaction, often demonstrating remarkable capabilities in generalisation and adaptability. At the same time, classical methods—rooted in well-established control theory, model-based planning, and rule-based systems—continue to offer reliability, interpretability, and formal guarantees that remain essential in safety-critical applications. This evolving landscape raises fundamental questions about when and how AI-driven approaches should complement or replace traditional techniques, and whether hybrid models combining classical and AI-based methods can leverage the strengths of both paradigms. Furthermore, while established metrics and evaluation frameworks exist for classi

title: Beyond the single neuron: computational principles of distributed neural coding in the age of large-scale recordings
summary: Neural coding is the fundamental language of the brain, the set of rules by which stimulus features and internal states are transformed into electrical signals. Historically, research focused on the properties of single neurons, emphasizing firing rates and receptive field tuning. However, a major paradigm shift is underway, moving toward the study of distributed representations where information is encoded in the collective activity of large-scale neural ensembles. From the precision of spike-timing, to the robustness of population vectors and high-dimensional manifolds, the principles governing neural representation are remarkably diverse. The central problem this Research Topic addresses is the absence of a unified theoretical framework bridging microscopic neural activity and macroscopic functional representations. While detailed models of single-cell biophysics and high-level descriptions of population dynamics exist, the "translation rules" between these scales remain elusive. Sp

title: Multimodal Annotation for Intangible Cultural Heritage: Embodied Knowledge and Technology
summary: The field of Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH) preservation increasingly depends on multimodal data, ranging from motion capture to volumetric video and sensory recordings, yet current digital documentation still reflects a largely product-oriented paradigm. This approach privileges outcomes rather than the creative, embodied, and processual dimensions of transmission. Recent research across digital humanities, performance studies, and human-computer interaction calls for a process-oriented shift that understands multimodal annotation not simply as record-keeping, but as a dynamic, interpretative practice. Landmark projects such as TKB, BlackBox, Motion Bank, and Arvest have illustrated how digital notebooks and hybrid archives can encode tacit knowledge, making performance and creative practices computationally addressable while preserving their embodied nature. Despite these advances, persistent challenges remain: the separation of data silos across modalities (e.g., video, text, se
image_alt: Multimodal Annotation for Intangible Cultural Heritage: Embodied Knowledge and Technology

title: Social Isolation, Social Participation, and Health Outcomes in Older Adults
summary: Research on ageing populations increasingly highlights the profound effects of social connectedness on health and well-being in later life. Social isolation is recognized as a significant risk factor for a range of adverse health outcomes among older adults, including cognitive decline, cardiovascular disease, depression, and reduced quality of life. While social participation is frequently associated with more positive physical and psychological outcomes, the mechanisms linking these factors remain insufficiently explored. The rapid uptake of digital technology, particularly smartphones, introduces both opportunities and challenges to the social integration of older people. Despite a growing body of research, much of the current literature is fragmented and lacks a holistic view of how overlapping social, technological, and psychological variables interact to shape health trajectories among older adults.
image_alt: Social Isolation, Social Participation, and Health Outcomes in Older Adults
